title: Erik Satie's birth chart
metaDescription: Erik Satie's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.3° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.7° separates Mercury and Uranus from an exact sextile; at that range thinking and disruption read as one mechanism. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 26.3° Taurus, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Taurus (1.1°), Venus in Gemini (16.7°), Mars in Aries (10.3°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction that begins as conversation, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mercury and Uranus: 0.7° from an exact sextile. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Mercury square Jupiter at 1.1°, and Mars conjunction Neptune at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Saturn while both square Jupiter. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks one placement here. Mars in Aries at 10.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 3 earth, 2 air, 2 fire, 2 water; by modality, 5 fixed, 3 cardinal, 1 mutable. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. Saturn was retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.5° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
